Fashion designs can be protected under copyright law, provided they demonstrate a sufficient amount of original creativity. [d5] The U.S. [d5] Copyright Office recognizes that fashion designs can qualify as protectable pictorial, graphic, or sculptural works, whether fixed on fabric or other tangible media [d1][d3], and copyright protection can extend to graphic designs, textile patterns, and artistic craftsmanship [d5][d1]. However, the scope of protection is nuanced: clothing designs are generally not protected unless they incorporate pictorial or graphic features that can be identified independently from their utilitarian function [d4][d2], and the U.S. [d5] does not accord fashion design the same broad protection as other creative works like art or film [d2][d3]. Instead, fashion designs are primarily protected under a separate sui generis regime — the Vessel Hull Design Protection Act (VH DPA) — which offers distinct, limited protection for qualifying designs [d3], while trademark law steps in to protect logos, labels, and brand elements that signify source or origin [d4].
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
